name: security-neo4j-procedure-authority-review
intent: Neo4j procedure/function execution and graph privilege delegation
artifacts: Procedure allow/unrestricted settings, execute/boosted privileges, procedure implementation and graph policy.
trace: Trace caller-controlled parameters through a permitted procedure into graph, file, network or process capabilities beyond the caller role.
experiment: Use an isolated synthetic graph and reviewed inert procedure; compare ordinary graph access with a forbidden delegated operation.
disproof: Procedure installation or an allowlist entry is not an exploit without caller reachability and a protected consumer.
repair: Constrain procedure implementation and execution privileges, verifying legitimate graph functionality and rejected delegation.
branch_decisions: Resolve database/graph privileges alongside EXECUTE PROCEDURE/FUNCTION, boosted execution and procedure allowlist/unrestricted settings. A procedure name alone does not establish filesystem/network capability. Inspect its implementation and the effective caller role; compare an intentionally allowed read-only procedure with the restricted operation in an isolated graph fixture.
operational_method: Retain the procedure signature/mode, installed implementation and effective grants. Ordinary EXECUTE permits invocation under applicable caller privileges; EXECUTE BOOSTED governs elevation and does not itself permit invocation. Elevated execution needs both grants for that procedure, subject to the deployed deny/mode rules. Separately, unrestricted registration is a configuration/implementation trust decision, not the user invocation grant. Compare invocation denied, ordinary execution and authorized boosted execution on an owned graph/trace; a procedure name or loading flag alone proves no file/network capability.
